title: The trouble lane's live verb answers with a summary row per trouble
intention: cairn/devices/trouble's bus verb `live` answers {'troubles': [ {id, standing, why, count, first_seen, last_seen} per live trouble ]}, with no occurrences or detail, so a reply's size grows with the number of live troubles and never with their history; the full record of one trouble stays reachable through the lane's own CLI (cairn trouble show / the store file).
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. This ticket closes live trouble /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/chat-pane-is-unbounded.json, a measured fault that enters as a bug (skills/intent/SKILL.md: a bug enters as a ticket, not through /intent). Measured 2026-10-10 by the builder at a43109013780's PROVED (cairn 20658ba6): of the newest 200 personal messages to cairn, 199 are trouble records, each a whole-store snapshot (~355 KB, body {'troubles': ...}), ~4,474 such messages, ~1.5 GB in the bus. cc0 traced the emitter: cairn/devices/cairn/device.py _trouble_pane_data asks the trouble lane `live` over the bus on EVERY render of cairn's page, and cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py _handle_live answers {'troubles': self.live()}, every live trouble with every occurrence; the reply is a personal message to cairn and the bus keeps it (Law 7). cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py _handle_ws_troubles asks the same verb. Both callers keep only id, standing, why, count (cairn also first_seen, last_seen).
traces_to: Law 7 (the record keeps everything, so what is posted must be what is meant); CP4 (each page render wrote ~355 KB to the bus forever); RULE 1 (the answer is the lane's public interface; its store stays its own).
how: cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py only: _handle_live returns summary dicts built from self.live() with exactly the six keys (a module tuple LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS = ('id','standing','why','count','first_seen','last_seen')). Python callers of TroubleDevice.live() (operator_inbox, codemother dashboard) are untouched: only the bus verb narrows. Update the verb's docstring with the measurement. Do NOT delete the ~4,474 snapshot messages already in the bus: that is Akien's call on a record of truth, and it is reported to him, not done here.
falsifier: cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_live_answers_a_summary.py under PROVES {'fa9a2703a9c3': {'1','2'}} on a scratch trouble store holding 3 live troubles of 50 occurrences each: (1) _handle_live({}) answers 3 rows, each with exactly LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS and the store's values for them; (2) the JSON of that answer is under 4 KB, and adding 50 more occurrences to each leaves its size unchanged. Hollow: returning self.live() reds both. Live check in the verdict: the newest trouble-reply message to cairn on the bus after one GET /device/cairn is under 16 KB.
watchme: none, because the fault was measured by the builder at a43109013780's PROVED (its trouble /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/chat-pane-is-unbounded.json, now cleared) and this ticket's verdict re-measures the live page; a recurrence shows in that pane's own size and load time
intent_berth: none, because this is a bug entering as a ticket (skills/intent/SKILL.md, the TICKET entry point), born from the measured fault at /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/chat-pane-is-unbounded.json

decisions.text: Narrow the verb rather than make cairn's page stop asking: asking over the bus is RULE 1's answer (ticket 9579a6f9cec6), and both callers already use only the summary keys. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
The snapshots already in the bus stay: deleting from a record of truth is not a builder's act; cc0 reports the 1.5 GB to Akien. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Step 1: write cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_live_answers_a_summary.py with two teeth (rows carry exactly the six keys and the store's values; the JSON is under 4 KB and its size is unchanged after 50 more occurrences), run it red before the build. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Step 2: in cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py add module tuple LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS = ('id','standing','why','count','first_seen','last_seen') and make _handle_live return {'troubles': [{k: t.get(k) for k in LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS} for t in self.live()]}; docstring records the measured reply size. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The proof's fixture is TroubleDevice(root=<tempdir>) with set_diagnostic_receiver(None), raising each of 3 idents 50 times via dev.raise_trouble(ident, why=..., detail={...~200 bytes...}); tooth 1 compares _handle_live({})['troubles'] to dev.live() on the six keys; tooth 2 compares JSON sizes before and after 50 more raises. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Step 3: no hand restart: the bus server answers stale when any *.py under the root changed (server.py answer()), and the client restarts it, so the first request after the build loads the new trouble shim; criterion 2 renders http://localhost/device/cairn once and reads the newest trouble reply to cairn. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
decisions.step: restart the trouble host and bus before validating criterion 2
